policies.name: Karnataka GCC Policy 2024-29
incentives: Innovation Labs/CoEs: govt funds up to 40% of capex, max INR 5 crore (Bengaluru Urban); up to 75% of capex, max INR 3 crore Beyond Bengaluru
Rental reimbursement (Beyond Bengaluru, first year): 50% of rent up to INR 50 lakh (100+ employees) or up to INR 2 crore (500+ employees)
Recruitment assistance (Beyond Bengaluru): 10-50% of recruitment cost by hiring slab, caps INR 35 lakh to INR 7 crore; customised package for 1,000+ hires
EPF reimbursement (Beyond Bengaluru, new GCCs with 100+ staff): up to INR 3,000/month/employee for 2 years, for up to 30% of workforce (max 250 employees)
R&D infrastructure grant: up to 40% of approved budget or INR 50 crore, whichever is lower (max 3 GCCs Beyond Bengaluru)
Skilling: 20% reimbursement up to INR 36,000 per graduate / INR 18,000 per diploma holder; internship stipend 50% up to INR 5,000/month for 3 months
100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years; 30% property tax reimbursement for 3 years; 25% of internet expenses up to INR 12 lakh/yr for 3 years (Beyond Bengaluru)
Co-working seats Beyond Bengaluru: 75%/50%/25% of vacant seat cost over 3 years, max INR 6,000/seat and INR 2.16 crore per applicant
Startups using GCC labs: 100% reimbursement up to INR 40 lakh per GCC; quality certification 50% up to INR 6 lakh; patent fees 50% up to INR 2 lakh (domestic)
policies.targets: 500 new GCCs (1,000 total) by 2029, 3.5 lakh new jobs, US$50 billion economic output
policies.summary: Announced in November 2024 and described as India's first dedicated GCC policy, it aims to double Karnataka's GCC base to 1,000 by 2029. Most cost-side incentives (rent, EPF, recruitment, power, property tax) are reserved for 'Beyond Bengaluru' clusters, while Bengaluru gets innovation-lab, skilling and R&D support.

policies.name: Maharashtra GCC Policy 2025
incentives: Capital subsidy: 20% of eligible fixed capital investment, capped at INR 10 crore (Small) / 20 crore (Medium) / 50 crore (Large) / 100 crore (Mega), paid in 5 instalments
Rental assistance (new units, 5 years, in lieu of capital subsidy): 10% of rent in Zone I (MMR/PMR), 20% in Zone II; caps INR 1-4 crore by unit size
Payroll subsidy (3 years): 40% of salary (Zone I) / 50% (Zone II), max INR 50,000 per employee, 100 employees, INR 5 crore per unit; employees earning > INR 1 lakh/month
Stamp duty exemption: 100% (SEZ/STPI), 75% (public IT park), 50% (private IT park)
Power tariff subsidy INR 1/unit (Zone I) or INR 2/unit (other zones) for 5 years, cap INR 20 lakh/unit/year; 100% electricity duty exemption for 10 years
R&D grant 25% up to INR 2 crore; patent filing 50% up to INR 50 lakh; internship support up to INR 10,000/month per intern (max 100)
Interest subsidy (Zone II only, 5 years): interest above 5% on term loans, yearly cap INR 5 crore
Non-fiscal: industry status, 24x7 operations, 10% of new MIDC land reserved for GCCs, additional FSI; customised package for >INR 750 crore or >1,000 jobs
policies.targets: 400 new GCCs, 4 lakh high-skilled jobs and INR 50,600 crore investment (2025-2030)
policies.summary: Approved by the state cabinet in September 2025, the policy offers size-graded capital, rental, payroll and power incentives to GCCs. Zone II (outside Mumbai and Pune) gets higher rental and payroll rates plus an interest subsidy, to push growth into Nagpur, Nashik and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
